Turner *sphuṭyati explicitly records the regional phuṭ-/phūṭ- break/burst verb, including Oriya phuṭibā, Gujarati phuṭvũ and Marathi phuṭṇẽ. These broken-state responses are its ordinary participial/past forms, retaining regional deaspiration and l-past or -ta endings. Both alternatives in the selected paired responses express the same verb family.

Turner bhaṅga explicitly gives Bengali bhāṅā to be broken, Oriya bhāṅgibā to break and Gujarati bhā̃gũ broken to pieces. These eastern and western broken-state forms are compared with that nasal bhaṅg- family, with ordinary past/stative suffixes and local reductions preserved. They are kept distinct from the unnasalized bhagna branch of bhajyate.

Turner *bhañjati explicitly records Nepali bhā̃cnu break and neighbouring Kumauni bhā̃cṇo. These Nepal/Tharu broken-state responses fit that affricate family, including ordinary -ko/-l- participles and the survey’s ts notation; they are not merged with the distinct nasal-velar bhaṅga family.
The whole completed-action phrase is break/burst + gone, phuṭ-/phūṭ- plus gay-/gal-. Turner *sphuṭyati and gata provide both lexical members; regional inflection and fusion are retained.
The full phrase is the eastern bhaṅg- break verb plus gal-/gone. Turner bhaṅga and gata supply the members, with the ordinary eastern participial construction represented in full.

The complete western broken-state phrase is bhāg-/broken + gone. Turner’s bhagna branch explicitly includes Gujarati bhāgũ broken and bhāgvũ break; gata supplies gay-/gy-. This is distinguished from the nasal bhaṅg- stem and from the related runaway sense.
The full eastern phrase is bhaṅg- broken, with its l-past form, plus ach-/ace present copula. Both the bhaṅga verb family and the ākṣeti copula family are linked.
